# Kassey's Kitchen

> Home bakery in Fullerton, CA. Cookies, banana bread, chocolate conchas, mini cake loaves, cookie party favor bags and dessert catering, made from scratch to order in small batches. Pickup details are confirmed with your order; the exact address is shared then.

## Menu and prices
- Brownie Cookies: $5 for 2
- Chocolate Chip Cookies: $5 for 2
- Mini Banana Bread: $5 each
- Large Banana Bread Loaf: $25
- Chocolate Conchas: $5 each
- Mini Cake Loaves: $5 each (ask about flavors)
- Cookie Party Favor Bags: $5.50 per bag, 2 cookies per bag, minimum 20 bags
- Sweet Treat Table (20 to 40 guests): starting at $250
- Full Dessert Catering (50+ guests): custom quote

## Ordering
- Orders start as a request through the order form; Kassey replies within 24 to 48 hours to confirm details, pricing and the date.
- Lead time: at least 3 to 5 days; catering and large orders at least 2 weeks.
- Pickup details are confirmed with your order. Delivery is available for catering orders for an additional fee.
- Payment: Venmo, Zelle, Apple Cash, Cash App, PayPal, cash. A deposit may be required for custom or catering orders.
- Allergens: made in a home kitchen that handles nuts, dairy, wheat and eggs.
- Contact: galavizkassey@gmail.com
- Instagram: @kasseyskitchen (https://www.instagram.com/kasseyskitchen/)

How catering booking works

Contact Kassey

Chat with Kassey
She reaches out within 48 hours to go over options, customize your menu and quote.

Lock it in
A deposit secures your date. Full payment is due 3 days before your event.

Delivered fresh
Everything arrives fresh and styled on the day of your event. You just enjoy it.

Lead time, pickup and delivery

Please book at least 2 weeks before your event. Weekends fill up fast, so book early. Pickup is free, and delivery is available for catering orders for an additional fee.

Catering questions
How far ahead should I book dessert catering?
At least 2 weeks before your event. Weekends fill up fast, so book early.

Do you deliver catering?
Yes. Delivery is available for catering orders for an additional fee. Pickup is free.

How does payment work for catering?
A deposit secures your date and full payment is due 3 days before your event. Kassey accepts Venmo, Zelle, Apple Cash, Cash App, PayPal and cash.

Can the desserts match my theme?
Yes. All packages are fully customizable, and the sweet treat table is styled to your theme.

Everything is made in a home kitchen that handles nuts, dairy, wheat and eggs, so allergen-free products cannot be guaranteed. Mention any allergies in your order request.

## About Kassey | Kassey's Kitchen, Fullerton, CA

https://kasseykitchen.com/about/

Home
About

Meet Kassey

Kassey's Kitchen is a home bakery in Fullerton, CA, sharing sweet handmade creations with the community.

From the heart of a home kitchen

Baking has always been my love language. What started as making treats for family gatherings quickly turned into something I knew I had to share more widely. There is something so meaningful about creating food that brings people joy.

My kitchen is small, my batches are intentional, and every order gets my full heart. Everything is made from scratch, baked fresh for your date, and never mass-produced.

What makes Kassey's Kitchen different

Made with love
Every item is handmade from scratch with quality ingredients. No shortcuts, no mixes, no freezer.

Small-batch quality
Limited orders mean every batch gets full attention. You are never one of thousands.

Community first
Proud to bake for neighbors in Fullerton.

Related See the menu, dessert catering, or how ordering works.

Pickup details are confirmed with your order. The exact address is shared when your order is confirmed.
Individual orders are pickup only. Delivery is available for catering orders for an additional fee.

## Ordering FAQ | Kassey's Kitchen, Fullerton, CA

https://kasseykitchen.com/faq/

Home
FAQ

Questions About Ordering

Everything you need to know before ordering from Kassey's Kitchen, a home bakery in Fullerton, CA.

Frequently asked questions
How far ahead do I need to order?
For most orders, allow at least 3 to 5 days. For catering and large orders, book at least 2 weeks ahead. Weekends fill up fast.

Where do I pick up my order?
Pickup details are confirmed with your order. Kassey's Kitchen is a home bakery, so the exact pickup address is shared once your order is confirmed.

Do you deliver?
There is no standard delivery for individual orders. Delivery is available for catering orders, and delivery fees may apply depending on distance.

How much do your baked goods cost?
Brownie cookies and chocolate chip cookies are $5 for 2. Mini banana bread, chocolate conchas and mini cake loaves are $5 each. The large banana bread loaf is $25. Sweet treat tables start at $250, cookie party favor bags are $5.50 each, and full dessert catering is quoted per event.

What payment methods do you accept?
Venmo, Zelle, Apple Cash, Cash App, PayPal and cash. A deposit may be required for custom or catering orders to secure your date.

Is my order confirmed when I send the form?
Not yet. The form sends a request. Kassey replies within 24 to 48 hours to finalize details, pricing and your date.

Do you accommodate allergies or dietary restrictions?
Everything is made in a home kitchen that handles nuts, dairy, wheat and eggs, so allergen-free products cannot be guaranteed. Always mention any allergies in your order request.

What events do you cater?
Birthday parties, baby showers, bridal showers, quinceañeras, corporate events, graduation parties, weddings and holiday parties. Book at least 2 weeks before your event.

Is everything made from scratch?
Yes. Every item is handmade from scratch in small batches. No shortcuts, no mixes, no freezer.

Related Still have questions? Contact Kassey, or see the menu and dessert catering.

Helpful guides What to Ask a Home Baker Before Ordering Event Desserts

Send a request and Kassey will reply within 24 to 48 hours.

## Desserts for an Office Holiday Party in Fullerton

https://kasseykitchen.com/blog/desserts-for-office-holiday-party-fullerton/

Home
Blog
Desserts for an Office Holiday Party in Fullerton

Desserts for an Office Holiday Party in Fullerton

Published October 24, 2026

Planning desserts for an office holiday party in Fullerton means thinking about lead time, the request process, and pickup before the week of the event. Kassey's Kitchen, a home bakery in Fullerton, CA, bakes brownie cookies, chocolate chip cookies, mini banana bread, large banana bread loaves, chocolate conchas, and mini cake loaves from scratch in small batches. Every order is made fresh to your date, and pickup details are confirmed with your order. This guide walks through what to order, how far ahead to plan, and what to expect from the request process.

Office party dessert order flow
--------------------------------
1. Send an order request at
https://kasseykitchen.com/order/
2. Kassey replies within 24 to 48
hours to confirm details, pricing,
and the date
3. Pickup details confirmed
with your order; address
shared after confirmation
4. Catering delivery may be available
for an additional fee, which may
depend on distance
How a Kassey's Kitchen order moves from request to pickup or catering delivery

Why Fullerton Offices Need a Dessert Game Plan

Kassey's Kitchen is a home bakery in Fullerton, CA. The exact pickup address is shared after your order is confirmed. Every order starts as a request through the order form. A request is not a confirmed order. Kassey replies within 24 to 48 hours to confirm details, pricing, and the date.

For a regular office party order, you need at least 3 to 5 days of lead time. For catering or large orders, give at least 2 weeks. Weekends fill up fast, so if your holiday party falls on a Friday or a weekend, send your request early. Individual orders are pickup only. Catering orders can include delivery for an additional fee, which may depend on distance.

A clear game plan means you know what you want, you send a request with enough lead time, and you confirm the pickup date before the party.

Desserts for an Office Holiday Party in Fullerton: Menu Options

Kassey's Kitchen offers a focused menu of baked goods that work well for an office setting. Here is the full list with prices.

Item
Price
Notes for an office party

Brownie cookies

You can read more about the cookies, banana bread, chocolate conchas, and mini cake loaves on their own pages. Every item is handmade from scratch. No shortcuts, no mixes, no freezer. Kassey bakes fresh for your specific date.

For an office holiday party, individual items are the easiest to set out. Mini banana bread, chocolate conchas, and mini cake loaves are grab and go. Cookies come two for $5, so you can order several sets without much math. The large banana bread loaf is a good centerpiece if you have a knife and a cutting board at the office.

Cookie party favor bags are a separate option. Each bag costs $5.50 and holds two cookies. The bag is kraft paper with a ribbon and a custom tag that carries your message. The minimum order is 20 bags. That works well if you want each coworker to leave with a small treat instead of a shared dessert table.

Fresh Baked Desserts for Pickup

Everything is made fresh to order and baked fresh for your date.

Ask Kassey how to transport and store the items in your order.

Because everything is fresh, plan your pickup so you can get the desserts to the office before you plan to serve them. Kassey will confirm the pickup address only after your order is confirmed, so you will know where to go.

Individual Items for a Simple Setup

## How to Keep Conchas Fresh for the Next Day

How to Keep Conchas Fresh for the Next Day

How to Keep Conchas Fresh for the Next Day

Published October 24, 2026

Knowing how to keep conchas fresh for the next day comes down to controlling air, moisture and starch staling. A chocolate concha from Kassey's Kitchen is a Mexican bakery classic with a chocolate twist: soft sweet bread topped with a crispy chocolate shell. That shell loses its snap when it sits in open air, and the crumb underneath dries out. You can slow both changes with the right container and a little planning.

SEND A REQUEST
|
v
KASSEY REPLIES WITHIN 24 TO 48 HOURS
|
v
CONFIRM DETAILS, PRICING AND DATE
|
+---- PICKUP (DETAILS CONFIRMED WITH YOUR ORDER)
|
+---- CATERING DELIVERY (FOR CATERING ORDERS)
How a Kassey's Kitchen concha order flows.

Why Conchas Go Stale Overnight

Conchas are enriched sweet breads. The soft crumb gets much of its tenderness from fat, sugar and water. Once the bread leaves the oven, moisture starts moving out of the crumb and into the air. The sugar shell on top pulls in moisture from the crumb or the room, and the shell can turn soft, sticky or cracked.

The main enemy overnight is starch retrogradation. As the baked starch cools and sits, the starch molecules recrystallize and squeeze out water. That is why bread firms up and tastes dry even inside a closed bag. The crust and shell lose their crispness for a different reason: humidity softens them. A good storage method has to protect the crumb from drying out while keeping the shell from getting soggy.

Freshness also depends on how the concha starts. Kassey's Kitchen bakes chocolate conchas from scratch in small batches, so they start with a fresh crumb and a crisp shell. The storage choices you make right after pickup decide how much of that freshness carries into the next day.

How to Keep Conchas Fresh for the Next Day: Best Storage Methods

For a one night hold, room temperature is the better place. The refrigerator speeds up staling, and a freezer is more than you need for something you will eat within 24 hours. The main choice is how tightly to close the container.

Tight method: Place conchas in a resealable bag or airtight container and press out air. This keeps the crumb soft, but the shell may soften. Reheat before serving to firm it up.

Loose method: Place conchas in a paper bag and fold the top down. This protects them from dust and moving air while letting some moisture escape. The shell stays crisper, but the crumb may dry slightly faster.

For most home kitchens, the tight method works well for next day eating. Plan to reheat in a low oven for a few minutes, which brings the shell closer to fresh.

Ask Kassey how to store and reheat your order.

Room Temperature Storage: The Counter Method

Cool conchas completely before sealing them. If they are still warm, trapped steam will make the shell gummy. That can happen with any concha, including one picked up fresh from a home bakery.

Lay a sheet of wax paper or parchment on the counter. Put one concha on each sheet and wrap loosely. Then place the wrapped conchas in a resealable bag or a container with a lid. Do not stack them tightly if the shell is still delicate, because the chocolate topping can crack or stick.

Store the bag or container in a cool spot away from direct sunlight and heat. A counter, bread box or a corner of the kitchen away from the stove works. Do not leave the bag open.

Eat or reheat within 24 hours for the best texture. After that, move any leftovers to the freezer.

Refrigerator vs. Freezer: What Actually Works

The refrigerator is not your friend for short term concha storage. Temperatures around 40 degrees Fahrenheit speed up starch retrogradation, which is the same process that makes bread feel stale. A concha stored in the fridge overnight can turn firm and dry even if it is wrapped.

Use the fridge only if the room is very warm and you are more worried about mold than texture. In that case, wrap each concha tightly in plastic wrap and place it in a sealed container. Reheat gently before eating and accept that the shell will need help crisping.

The freezer is the better choice for anything longer than a day or two. Wrap each concha individually in plastic wrap, then place the wrapped pieces in a freezer-safe bag. Press out air before sealing. Frozen conchas keep well for a few weeks, but eating them sooner is better.

When you want one, pull it from the freezer and let it sit at room temperature while the oven preheats, or heat it directly from frozen for a little longer.

How to Reheat Conchas Without Drying Them Out

Reheating restores some of the fresh-baked contrast between a soft crumb and a firmer shell. A low oven works better than a microwave, which can make the crumb tough and chewy.

Heat the oven or toaster oven to 300 degrees Fahrenheit.

Place conchas on a baking sheet. If the shell is already dark or cracked, cover it loosely with foil.

Heat for 5 to 7 minutes for a room temperature concha.

For a frozen concha, heat for 8 to 10 minutes, or thaw first for 15 to 20 minutes at room temperature.

Let it cool for 2 to 3 minutes before eating. The shell will firm up slightly as it cools.

Only reheat what you plan to eat. Repeated reheating dries out the crumb and can make the shell tough.

Make Ahead Tips for Bakery Fresh Conchas at Home

If you want Kassey's chocolate conchas ready for a Sunday morning, work backward from the pickup date. Kassey's Kitchen asks for at least 3 to 5 days of lead time on regular orders, and weekends fill up fast. You submit a request through the order form, and Kassey replies within 24 to 48 hours to confirm the details, pricing and date. Pickup details are confirmed with your order. A request is not a confirmed order until she confirms it.

Here is a simple one night example:

Send an order request on Tuesday for a Saturday pickup.

Pick up chocolate conchas, which are $5 each.

Serve the conchas with coffee or hot chocolate.

For larger event planning, the same storage rules apply. If you need a dessert spread for an office event, read desserts for an office holiday party in Fullerton. You can also check the current Kassey's Kitchen menu for items and pricing.

Do not try to keep a concha fresh for days in a paper bag. It will dry out. A sealed container or freezer is the reliable route.

Frequently asked questions

Can I refrigerate conchas overnight?

You can, but it is usually not the ideal choice. Refrigerator temperatures encourage staling in enriched breads. If you must refrigerate, wrap each concha tightly and reheat gently before serving.

Should I freeze conchas to keep them fresh?

Yes, if you will not eat them within a day or two. Wrap each concha in plastic wrap, put the wrapped pieces in a freezer-safe bag, and press out extra air. Thaw at room temperature or heat directly from frozen.

How do I reheat conchas without drying them out?

Use a 300 degree Fahrenheit oven or toaster oven for 5 to 7 minutes. Cover loosely with foil if the shell is already dark. Avoid the microwave because it can make the crumb tough.

Why did my conchas turn hard?

They lost moisture to the air and staled. Store them in a sealed bag or container soon after they cool, and reheat before serving to soften the crumb and re-crisp the shell.

Planning a Dessert Table for a Graduation Party

Planning a Dessert Table for a Graduation Party

Published October 24, 2026

Planning a graduation dessert table starts with one simple question: how much will people actually eat? Most hosts overthink the count and underthink the flow. A graduation dessert table works best when it is easy to approach, easy to serve, and easy to clean up. You want a small lineup of items that hold up well at room temperature and taste good after sitting out for an hour or two. You also want a table that looks intentional in photos without requiring you to stand next to it all night. The details below will help you build that table without stress.

GRADUATION DESSERT TABLE ORDER FLOW
-----------------------------------
1. Send an order request. [request form]
2. Kassey replies within 24 to 48 hours. [confirm details]
3. Pickup OR catering delivery. [depends on order]
-----------------------------------
Lead time: 3 to 5 days for regular orders.
Lead time: 2 weeks for catering and large orders. Order flow for a graduation dessert table

How to Plan a Graduation Dessert Table

The number that matters is not a strict count. It is variety plus visual fullness. A table with three different items looks fuller than a table with many of one item. For a graduation party with 20 to 40 guests, the Sweet Treat Table from Kassey's Kitchen is a practical starting point. It includes a spread of two to three baked goods styled to the event theme, a cookie assortment, and custom signage. That gives you enough variety to make the table feel decorated without forcing you to manage a long list of trays.

For a larger graduation party of 50 or more guests, full dessert catering is the better fit. Kassey builds a multi-item custom menu, delivers it, sets up the table, and adds custom signage. Full Dessert Catering is custom quoted for 50+ guests. All catering packages are fully customizable, and they are starting points. The important planning rule is to finalize this early. Catering and large orders need at least two weeks of lead time, and weekends fill up fast in graduation season.

If you are picking up individual items instead of booking a package, keep the table simple. Two or three items are enough for most parties. Brownie cookies give you texture. Chocolate chip cookies give you a familiar favorite. Mini banana bread or mini cake loaves give the table height and variety. A table with four trays of the same cookie looks boring. A table with three distinct items looks curated.

Choosing a Theme and Color Palette for Your Dessert Table

Your dessert table should match the graduate's school colors or party theme. The easiest way to do that is through napkins, signage, table runners, and serving trays, not through artificial food coloring on every dessert. The baked goods themselves can stay natural and simple. The surrounding decor carries the color.

Graduation tables tend to use school colors aggressively. That is fine, but the table reads better in photos when one neutral color breaks it up. A wooden board, a white platter, or kraft paper packaging can do that. Cookie party favor bags from Kassey's Kitchen already use kraft bags with ribbon and a custom tag. If you order favor bags for a graduation party, you can put the graduate's name, graduation year, or a short message on the tag. Cookie party favor bags are $5.50 per bag. The minimum is 20 bags, and each bag holds two cookies.

For the table itself, pick one focal point. A small chalkboard or printed sign near the center works better than banners hanging behind the table. Custom signage comes with the catering packages, which takes one task off your list. If you are handling decor yourself, put the sign at eye level and keep the wording short: the graduate's name and year is enough.

Must-Have Desserts for a Graduation Dessert Table

A graduation dessert table needs items that people can grab and eat while standing. That means no plates, no forks, no cutting, and no melting. The best fit from the Kassey's Kitchen menu is the cookie and mini loaf family.

Brownie cookies are a strong anchor for a graduation table. They are rich and fudgy with crisp edges and gooey centers. They feel more special than a standard brownie because the texture is somewhere between a brownie and a cookie. Brownie cookies are $5 for two.

Chocolate chip cookies are the reliable pick. They are thick, chewy, and loaded with semi-sweet chocolate chips. Every party has a few guests who want the familiar option, and this is it. Chocolate chip cookies are $5 for two.

Mini banana bread loaves add a different shape and a softer flavor. Mini banana bread is $5 each. The mini size is useful because guests can take one whole without feeling like they committed to a large slice. A large banana bread loaf is $25 if you prefer to slice and arrange the bread yourself on a tray.

Chocolate conchas are a Mexican bakery classic with a chocolate twist. The soft sweet bread has a crispy chocolate shell on top. They photograph beautifully and work well on a table with a graduation theme that leans into cultural traditions. Chocolate conchas are $5 each.

Mini cake loaves are $5 each. Flavors vary, so you will need to ask Kassey what is available around your party date. They give the table a cake presence in small, handheld form.

The best combination for a table is usually a cookie, a second cookie or concha, and a mini loaf or cake loaf. That gives you crunch, chew, softness, and visual height.

Budget-Friendly Graduation Dessert Table Planning Tips

The fastest way to overspend on a dessert table is to buy too many different items. Every extra variety means another tray, another price point, and more leftovers. A controlled table with three items often looks better and costs less than a sprawling table with six.

Start with pricing that fits your guest count. Brownie cookies and chocolate chip cookies are $5 for two. Mini banana bread, chocolate conchas, and mini cake loaves are $5 each. If you have 20 to 40 guests, a short list of three items such as one cookie option, one mini loaf option, and one concha option is a simple budget worksheet. For example, you might plan a pickup order with brownie cookies, mini banana bread, and chocolate conchas. List the number of each item in your request and Kassey will confirm details and pricing within 24 to 48 hours.

If you want grab-and-go favors instead of an open table, cookie party favor bags cost $5.50 per bag with a minimum of 20 bags, which gives guests a small, tidy package with custom tags.

For a hosted dessert table at a 20 to 40 guest graduation party, the Sweet Treat Table starts at $250. That includes the spread, cookie assortment, styling, and signage. For 50 or more guests, full dessert catering is custom quoted. Request a quote early and ask what fits your budget rather than guessing.

One more budget tip: do not double up on dessert if you are also serving another dessert from a family member. One strong dessert table is enough. If a relative insists on bringing a dessert, build your table around smaller handheld items so the two desserts do not compete.

Setup and Display Ideas That Photograph Well

Graduation dessert tables get photographed more than they get eaten in the first hour. People take pictures before they take a cookie. That means your display matters as much as your menu.

Use height. Put mini cake loaves and mini banana breads on a small riser, a wooden crate, or a stack of books covered with a cloth. Flat trays of cookies sit in front. Conchas look best grouped on a round platter or cake stand. The height difference makes the table look fuller without adding more desserts.

Keep labels short. A small card that says "brownie cookies" or "chocolate conchas" is enough. Do not clutter the table with long descriptions. Custom signage is included; ask Kassey whether individual dessert labels are included.

Think about timing. Set the table up close to dessert time. That keeps the cookies and breads from sitting out too long. For pickup orders, keep everything in sealed containers until setup time.

Leave room for napkins and small plates if you serve the large banana bread loaf sliced. A stack of cocktail napkins near the table edge is enough for cookies and minis. Do not crowd the center with napkins; put them on one side.

For favor bags, line them up in rows on a side table rather than the main dessert table. The kraft bags with ribbon and custom tags will look like part of the decor, and guests can take one on the way out.
